title: Siege of Vienna 1529: How a baker's firebreak fooled the Ottomans
hook: A Viennese baker's secret firebreak turned the tide of the 1529 Ottoman siege.
description:

beats.say: The Ottoman cannons thundered, yet the real surprise was the Viennese baker's secret firebreak.
On September 27, 1529, Grand Vizier Ibrahim Pasha ordered the siege to begin before sunrise.
He expected the city walls to crumble, but the bakers had stacked barrels of flour, creating a smokescreen.
beats.visual: Ottoman artillery smoke barrels flour Vienna

beats.say: When the Janissaries advanced, the smoke choked their arquebuses, forcing a costly retreat.
Meanwhile, a hidden Swiss mercenary, Jakob von Habsburg, slipped through the tunnels to sabotage Ottoman gunpowder.
beats.visual: Jakob von Habsburg tunnel sabotage gunpowder

beats.say: He set off a small explosion that scattered the cannons, delaying the breach by two days.
The defenders seized the moment, launching a sudden sortie that seized the Ottoman supply wagons.
Caught without food, the siege army fell into panic, and Ibrahim Pasha called off the attack on October 15.
History books praise the walls, but it was the baker's quick thinking that saved Vienna.
Thus, a humble oven became the hidden hero of the first siege of Vienna.
